title: ASME Audit Support in Chicago | Joint Review NDE Prep
description: ASME joint review prep for Chicago-area boiler, vessel and stainless process shops: NDE written practice, procedures, Illinois and city rules. Contact us.
h1: ASME Certification Audit Support in Chicago: NDE Preparation Under Two Jurisdictions
html:
Chicago-area manufacturers of heating boilers, water heaters, stainless process vessels and refinery equipment, and the repair organizations that keep the region's boiler rooms running, all face the same moment every three years: the ASME joint review. This page explains how an ASNT NDT Level III from Atlantis NDT gets the nondestructive examination part of your quality control system ready for it, and how the Illinois and City of Chicago rules frame the work. Atlantis is based in Houston and travels to Chicagoland for site work, with most document review done remotely. Ask about your review.

The Chicagoland pressure equipment base

The Chicago region builds a wider spread of pressure equipment than the Gulf Coast does. A city of large commercial and institutional buildings, with a long winter, supports manufacturers and assemblers of heating boilers and water heaters built to Section IV, where the H and HLW designators apply. Food, beverage, pharmaceutical and specialty chemical plants across northern Illinois buy stainless steel process vessels, jacketed kettles and tanks built to Section VIII Division 1. The refineries and petrochemical plants in the Joliet area and across the state line in northwest Indiana draw on exchanger, drum and piping fabricators. And a large population of boiler repair and service firms works under both state and city licenses, some of them holding the National Board R certificate.

That variety matters for the NDE side of the review. A Section IV boiler line, a sanitary stainless vessel shop and a carbon-steel refinery exchanger shop each lean on different examination methods, so the review team's questions about NDE differ from one certificate holder to the next. Our Chicago NDT consulting page covers the wider regional picture.

Illinois and the City of Chicago: two sets of rules

Illinois regulates boilers and pressure vessels statewide through the Office of the State Fire Marshal, Division of Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety, under its Chief Boiler Inspector. State law requires boilers and pressure vessels to be registered and inspected unless an exemption applies. Illinois adopts the ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code by reference for new construction, expects the appropriate Code symbol stamp on the nameplate, and does not permit non-Code boilers or pressure vessels to be installed and operated. The first inspection of new or used equipment is done by a state inspector, insurance company inspectors may inspect what their companies insure, and welded repairs to pressure equipment may be done only by a company licensed by the Division.

The City of Chicago is a separate National Board member jurisdiction. Its Department of Buildings runs a Boiler Inspection Bureau whose city inspectors inspect boilers and unfired pressure vessels in apartment buildings, commercial buildings, schools, churches, hospitals and nursing homes. New installations follow a permit, a first inspection and, for new or used units being installed and boilers after major repairs, a hydrostatic test witnessed by the Bureau. Repairs inside the city must be done by a boiler repairer licensed by the City of Chicago.

For a manufacturer, those layers mostly show up as delivery requirements: Code stamping, a Manufacturer's Data Report and National Board registration that will satisfy whichever jurisdiction receives the equipment. For a repair organization, they show up as licensing that must be in place before welding starts, in addition to any R certificate. Our Illinois NDT consulting page and Illinois inspection services page give more state context.

Section IV and Section VIII lines make different NDE demands

Heating boiler construction to Section IV relies far less on volumetric examination than Section VIII vessel work. A great deal of the assurance on an H-stamped boiler comes from qualified welding, visual examination by trained people and the hydrostatic test. That does not take NDE out of the joint review. The team still checks that visual examination is defined, that whoever performs it is qualified under the manufacturer's system, that any radiography or ultrasonic examination the design or a customer requires is controlled, and that the test gauges are calibrated. Shops that hold both H and U certificates need their quality control manual to keep the two sets of rules apart, so that a Section IV traveler never borrows a Section VIII acceptance standard or the reverse.

Section VIII stainless process vessels bring the familiar Division 1 examination rules: full or spot radiography of butt welds according to the joint efficiency chosen in design, ultrasonic examination where it replaces radiography or covers thick sections, and surface examination where the Code or the purchaser asks for it. The rules behind those choices are summarized in our Division 1 overview, with radiography technique covered in the Article 2 notes.

Refinery-corridor exchangers and drums

Fabricators who serve the refineries south and southeast of the city build carbon and low-alloy steel exchangers, drums and towers where examination is heavier: full radiography or ultrasonic examination in its place, magnetic particle examination of nozzle and attachment welds, hardness checks and positive material identification demanded by the refinery's own specifications. The Code part of that work and the refinery's additions should live in different columns of the traveler. When a review team samples one of these jobs, it wants to see which examinations the Code required, which the purchaser added, and that both were carried out by qualified people to accepted procedures. Thick nozzle forgings and tubesheets also bring ultrasonic examination of purchased material into the picture, which ties your NDE controls to your receiving inspection. Our refining NDT consulting page covers the owner side of that relationship.

Penetrant examination on stainless: details the team checks

Food and pharmaceutical vessel shops do a great deal of liquid penetrant work, and stainless steel makes the procedure details matter. Section V's penetrant article controls the contaminant content of penetrant materials used on austenitic stainless steel, titanium and nickel-base alloys, which means the shop needs the batch certifications for the penetrant, remover and developer actually in use, not just the product data sheet. The procedure has to define surface preparation on polished or ground welds, the temperature range, dwell times, how excess penetrant is removed without washing indications away, developer application and the minimum light intensity at the examination surface, with a calibrated meter to prove it.

Post-examination cleaning is a second issue unique to sanitary work. Residual penetrant or developer in a product-contact vessel is a contamination problem for the owner, so the procedure and the traveler should say how the part is cleaned afterward and who checks it. None of this is exotic, but a review team that finds an expired batch certification or a light meter last calibrated three years ago will write it up. See our Section V Article 6 page and penetrant testing of stainless steel for more on the method.

How Chicago-area shops staff NDE

Smaller boiler and vessel manufacturers around Chicago usually certify their own people for visual, penetrant and magnetic particle examination and buy radiography and ultrasonic work from the area's commercial NDE labs, of which the metro has many. An outside Level III often owns the written practice and gives the qualification examinations. Larger plants may have a staffed NDE group and an in-house Level III.

Either way, the pressure point is the same: the certificate holder has to show it controls examinations it did not perform. A lab's own accreditation or reputation is not a substitute for your acceptance of its procedures and personnel for your Code work. The team will ask for your records of that acceptance, and for evidence that someone in your organization reviewed the radiographs or UT data before the Authorized Inspector. If the lab rotates technicians through your jobs, each one must be covered, and their certifications must be valid on the dates they examined your welds.

A short list of what we check in that subcontractor file:

  • The lab's written practice, read against SNT-TC-1A or CP-189 as your Code edition and contract require.
  • Each procedure used on your welds, with Section V method article requirements met and your acceptance recorded.
  • A roster of the technicians who worked on your jobs since the last review, with certification and vision dates.
  • Calibration evidence for the lab's equipment where the Code or the procedure requires it.
  • Your reviewer's signature on each set of radiographs or UT reports, and that reviewer's qualification.

Our subcontractor approval audits page describes the full supplier-audit method.

Repair organizations and the R certificate in Chicago

Boiler repair firms in the Chicago area deal with three overlapping authorities: their National Board R certificate for repairs and alterations under NBIC Part 3, the State Fire Marshal's repair licensing for welded repairs in Illinois, and the city's repairer licensing inside Chicago. The NDE side of a repair is governed by the original code of construction and the NBIC, and the examination records go with the repair documentation. An R certificate review checks those controls in much the same spirit as an ASME joint review. Our NBIC R-stamp NDT audit support page and the NBIC NB-23 compliance guide explain that review.

Atlantis's role on a Chicago review, and its limits

For the NDE portion of your joint review, Atlantis reads your written practice and procedures, finds the gaps against Section V and the construction Code, and writes or rewrites what is missing through our written practice and procedure development services. We audit examiner files for training, experience, examinations and vision; prepare procedure demonstrations where the Code requires them; build the subcontractor file; draft NDE language for your manual; and run a mock review of the NDE portion with your staff before the team arrives. On site visits we also check your MT equipment, light meters, penetrant batch certifications and calibration records against the procedures that cite them.

Atlantis does not take on the roles that belong to others. We are not an Authorized Inspection Agency, we do not sign data reports, and ASME, not Atlantis, decides on your certificate. Welding documents (specifications, qualification records, welder qualifications) are produced by your welding engineer, never by Atlantis; the WPS, PQR and WPQ article shows how that paperwork connects to the stamp program. We do not support Section III nuclear certificates. Radiographic exposures are also outside our work in the US, so our reviews of a lab's radiography carry no commercial interest in its results.

Chicago readiness checklist for the NDE portion

  1. Confirm which certificates you hold (H, HLW, U or others) and that the manual keeps the Section IV and Section VIII NDE rules separate.
  2. Check the written practice for the Code edition, the SNT-TC-1A or CP-189 edition it references, the named Level III and the examination rules.
  3. For stainless work, collect the penetrant material batch certifications for every batch used since the last review.
  4. Check light meter, MT yoke and gauge calibration records against the procedures and the travelers that cite them.
  5. Build or update the subcontractor file for each NDE lab, including the technician roster for your jobs.
  6. Pick a recent H-stamped boiler and a recent U-stamped vessel and trace the examinations and tests from traveler to data report.
  7. Confirm state and city repair licensing is current if you do repair work, alongside any R certificate.
  8. Check that hydrostatic test records name the gauge and its calibration.
  9. Open a handful of randomly chosen jobs from the past three years and time how long it takes to produce their complete NDE records.
  10. Rehearse the interviews with the people who hold quality duties.

Shops that track certifications and calibrations by hand can see how a records system helps on our expired certifications page and our procedure control page.

What to send us

Email the designators on your certificate, the scope wording, the month your AIA expects the review, the examination, NDE, subcontracting and records sections of your manual, your written practice, your procedure index and your list of NDE labs. We return a gap list tied to manual paragraphs and Code requirements, then visit to sample records, walk the floor and run a mock review of the NDE portion. We reply within one business day. Technicians who need training before certification can use our NDT training for Chicago, built on SNT-TC-1A; certification itself remains your company's act under its written practice. The national ASME audit Level III support page sets out the complete service, and other Great Lakes manufacturers can read our Cleveland ASME audit support page.

faq.q: Do we answer to the State of Illinois or the City of Chicago?
faq.a: Equipment installed in Chicago falls under the city's Boiler Inspection Bureau, which is a separate National Board member jurisdiction; the rest of Illinois falls under the State Fire Marshal's Division of Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety. Manufacturers mainly feel this through stamping and registration requirements; repair firms feel it through licensing.

faq.q: We build only Section IV heating boilers. Is NDE even part of our joint review?
faq.a: Yes, though in a smaller way than for Section VIII. The team checks visual examination, examiner qualification, any radiography or UT the design or a customer requires, and the calibration of test gauges.

faq.q: What penetrant records do auditors ask for on stainless vessels?
faq.a: Contaminant certifications for each batch of penetrant, remover and developer used, the procedure with its dwell, temperature and lighting requirements, light meter calibration, examiner certifications and post-cleaning instructions. See Section V Article 6.

faq.q: Who certifies our in-house PT and MT examiners?
faq.a: Your company does, under its written practice, after the training, experience and examinations the practice requires. An outside Level III can write the practice and give the examinations. Our training records page lists the evidence.

faq.q: Can Atlantis audit our radiography lab?
faq.a: Yes. As an independent Level III we review the lab's written practice, procedures, technician certifications and the radiographs on your jobs. Atlantis takes no radiographs in the United States, so it has no interest in the lab's results.

faq.q: Does a Chicago boiler repairer license replace an R certificate?
faq.a: No. They answer different questions: one is the city's permission to repair inside Chicago, the other is National Board accreditation for repairs and alterations under the NBIC. Check with the Boiler Inspection Bureau and your AIA which a given job needs.

faq.q: How early should we start on the NDE side?
faq.a: Several months before the review. Rebuilding experience records, re-approving procedures and assembling subcontractor files all take longer than shops expect.

faq.q: Do you write our quality control manual?
faq.a: We draft the NDE content for your quality manager to adopt. Ownership of the manual never moves: it belongs to you, and acceptance comes from your Authorized Inspection Agency.

faq.q: Do you support Section III nuclear certificates?
faq.a: No. Section III nuclear work is outside our scope.
